analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page describes three branches of the federal government, their makeup and key roles, and the system of checks and balances between them.

overview.headline: three federal branches, their makeup, roles, and system of checks and balances

keyPoints.point: Constitution divides federal government into three branches to prevent concentrated power
keyPoints.quote: The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches:

keyPoints.point: legislative branch is made up of Congress including Senate and House with lawmaking duties
keyPoints.quote: The legislative branch is made up of Congress:

keyPoints.point: judicial branch evaluates laws by Interpreting the meaning of laws and deciding constitutionality
executive branch members include president and vice president and cabinet who serve as advisors
keyPoints.quote: The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch.

keyPoints.point: ability of each branch to respond to actions of other branches defines system of checks and balances
keyPoints.quote: The ability of each branch to respond to the actions of the other branches is the system of checks and balances.

keyTerms.gloss: branch that includes Congress and drafts proposed laws
branch that includes Supreme Court and evaluates laws
keyTerms.quote: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts.

keyTerms.gloss: branch led by president that includes cabinet and departments
keyTerms.quote: The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch.

keyTerms.gloss: document that divides federal government into three branches
keyTerms.quote: The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches:

keyTerms.gloss: system where each branch can respond to actions of other branches
keyTerms.quote: The ability of each branch to respond to the actions of the other branches is the system of checks and balances.

keyTerms.gloss: presidential power to reject legislation created by Congress
keyTerms.quote: The president can veto legislation created by Congress. He or she also nominates heads of federal agencies and high court appointees.
